Name: Add Senders to Exchange-Siemplify Inbox Rule
Author: admin
DisplayName: Add Senders to Exchange-Siemplify Inbox Rule
Description: Action will get as a parameter a list of Email Addresses, or will work on User entities with Email regexes (if parameters are not provided), and will be able to create a new rule, filtering the senders from your mailboxes. Actions can be modified in the parameters using the rule parameter. WARNING: Action will modify your current users inbox rules, using EWS. NOTICE - to perform operation, please configure EDiscovery Group and Author permissions. For full details, please visit: https://cloud.google.com/chronicle/docs/soar/marketplace-integrations/exchang. NOTE: Action is running as async, please adjust script timeout value in Siemplify IDE for action as needed.

Parameters.Description: Specify the Senders you would like to add to the rule, in a comma separated list. If no parameter will be provided, action will work with User entities.

Parameters.DefaultValue: Siemplify - Senders List - Move To Junk
Parameters.Description: Specify the rule to add the sender to. If the rule doesn't exist - action will create it where it's missing.
OptionalValues: Siemplify - Senders List - Move To Junk

Parameters.DisplayName: Should add senders' domain to the corresponding Domains List rule as well?
Parameters.Description: Specify whether the action should automatically take the domains of the provided email addresses and add them as well to the corresponding domain rules (same rule action for domains)

If checked, action will be performed in all mailboxes accessible with current impersonalization settings. If delegated access is used, implicitly specify the mailboxes to search in the "Mailboxes" parameter.

Parameters.DisplayName: How many mailboxes to process in a single batch
Parameters.Description: In case "Perform action in all mailboxes" is checked, action works in batches, this parameter controls how many mailboxes action should process in single batch (single connection to mail server).

AIDescription:
Adds specified email senders to Microsoft Exchange inbox rules to automate email filtering (e.g., moving to junk or deleting). The action can target specific email addresses provided as parameters or extract them from User entities in the case. It supports processing a single mailbox or all mailboxes accessible via the configured integration permissions. Additionally, it can optionally extract domains from the provided email addresses and add them to corresponding domain-based filtering rules.

### Parameters
| Parameter | Type | Mandatory | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Senders | String | No | A comma-separated list of email addresses to add to the rule. If not provided, the action will attempt to use the identifiers of User entities. |
| Rule to add senders to | Dropdown | Yes | The specific Exchange rule to update or create. Options include: 'Siemplify - Senders List - Move To Junk', 'Siemplify - Senders List - Delete', or 'Siemplify - Senders List - Permanently Delete'. |
| Should add senders' domain to the corresponding Domains List rule as well? | Boolean | No | If true, the action extracts the domain from each email and adds it to the equivalent domain-based rule (e.g., 'Siemplify - Domains List - Move To Junk'). |
| Perform action in all mailboxes | Boolean | No | If true, the action attempts to apply the rule changes to all searchable mailboxes in the Exchange environment. |
| How many mailboxes to process in a single batch | Integer | No | Controls the number of mailboxes processed in each iteration of this asynchronous action. Default is 50. |

### Flow Description
1. **Initialization**: The action initializes the Exchange manager using the integration's configuration (Server Address, Credentials, etc.).
2. **Sender Identification**: It retrieves the list of senders from the 'Senders' parameter. If empty, it collects identifiers from all 'USERUNIQNAME' entities in the current scope.
3. **Mailbox Discovery**: If 'Perform action in all mailboxes' is enabled, it fetches a list of all searchable mailboxes; otherwise, it uses the primary mailbox.
4. **Rule Processing**: For each mailbox in the current batch, the action checks for the existence of the target rule. 
5. **Mutation**: If the rule exists, it appends the new senders to the rule's conditions. If the rule does not exist, it creates a new rule with the specified action and senders.
6. **Domain Handling**: If requested, it repeats the logic for domain-based rules using the domains extracted from the sender list.
7. **Async Iteration**: If more mailboxes remain, the action saves its state and continues in the next iteration until all mailboxes are processed.
